stance_summary: Canada is too cheap versus the United States on a peer-normalized policy/2Y basis: CA-US 2Y at -140bp sits in the 4th percentile of both 1y and 5y history, and the 2027 H1 CORRA–SOFR strip prints the same ~140bp gap. That is not a fade-because-it-fell screen. The valuation anchor is the historical CA-US front-end spread plus comparable-country policy normalization after a delivered Fed hike, BoC energy pass-through minutes, and a still-156bp overnight CORRA (2.29) versus SOFR (3.85) gap. Convergence should begin now because the US 2Y already rerated to a 99.8th percentile 1y level after +57bp in a month, while Canada is only mid-range versus 5y history and still prices a structurally wide 2027 gap even after more CORRA hikes than SOFR hikes. Express it rates-first: long the SOFR–CORRA 2027 H1 implied-rate differential (receive SOFR / pay CORRA). Spot USDCAD is the same CAD-catch-up view but fights 140bp of 2Y carry and is only a 74th/87th percentile pair, so it is inferior.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Long SOFR 2027-03/2027-06 strip average versus short CORRA 2027-03/2027-06 strip average (receive SR3 / pay CRA), locking the 2027 H1 implied-rate differential that currently matches CA-US 2Y at about -140bp.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD (long CAD versus USD) at ECB-cross 1.401047 as of 2026-09-18.
expression_comparison.rationale: The dislocation is a peer policy/2Y spread, not a spot-PPP gap. Frozen STIR already prices the same ~140bp 2027 H1 gap as CA-US 2Y, so SOFR versus CORRA owns the mispricing directly. USDCAD is only 74th percentile 1y / 87th percentile 5y and the packet carry screen shows a 140bp 2Y yield differential supporting long USD/short CAD, so fading USDCAD fights carry and mixes USD idiosyncrasy. Rates are cleaner and executable from tradable_rate_curves.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Canada, an energy-exporting G10 peer, is running a structurally cheap policy setting versus the United States after a delivered Fed hike and with BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through. The closing mechanism is relative front-end repricing: CORRA implied rates rise versus SOFR as BoC catch-up and US 2Y already-extreme levels normalize the CA-US spread, rather than a generic USD-down or Canada-growth-up story.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified fact: official SOFR was 3.62 on 2026-09-16 and 3.85 on 2026-09-17 after the Fed raised 25bp to 3.75–4.00%; US 2Y is 4.76 as of 2026-09-18, +57bp 1m / +125bp 1y. CORRA is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17; CA 2Y is 3.27, +31bp 1m / +77bp 1y. CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 2026-09-17, -17bp 1m / -43bp 1y / -46bp 6m. SR3 2027-03/06 imply 4.58/4.72 (+73/+87bp from SOFR); CRA 2027-03/06 imply 3.13/3.365 (+84/+107.5bp from CORRA). USDCAD is 1.401047, +1.74% 1m. Known information (US inflation still firm, Canada labor softer) was already in the level; the marginal path is the post-FOMC US front-end rerating widening an already historically cheap Canada spread.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Canada headline CPI at 3% with core near 2%; US labor/inflation gauges still hot (75/72) versus Canada (38/55); Canada has been below the US on overnight and 2Y for months. New: the September 16 FOMC hike was >90% priced into the decision and has now printed, with SOFR jumping to 3.85; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; energy-market shock absorbers are weakening even as a Saudi Oman ship-to-ship workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; desk thesis is that the energy shock is constraining global easing. The known Canada-soft labor picture cannot by itself explain a new 5d CA-US 2Y move of -15bp (z -2.17) after a US hike that was already widely expected.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Pricing requires Canada to stay about 140bp cheap to the US through 2027 H1 even after CORRA prices more additional hikes than SOFR (CRA Sep-2027 +122bp versus SR3 Sep-2027 +90.5bp). Overnight CORRA-SOFR is 156bp (2.29 vs 3.85). That path assumes Canada core near 2% and labor weakness keep BoC structurally below the Fed, with energy pass-through remaining a minutes risk rather than a relative-rate event.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The 4th-percentile CA-US 2Y / 140bp 2027 H1 STIR gap is the wrong relative terminal. Peer normalization after a delivered Fed hike plus BoC energy pass-through should compress Canada cheapness versus the US by more than the residual 2027 gap still embedded in CRA versus SR3. Percentile is the discovery flag; the disagreed assumption is the priced structural 140bp Canada discount.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: CA 2Y 3.27 versus US 2Y 4.76; overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85. Change: US 2Y +9bp 1d / +57bp 1m; CA 2Y -8bp 1d / +31bp 1m, so the latest widening is a US rerating plus a Canada 1d yield dip, not a Canada collapse. Tenor: the 2Y/STIR window, not 10Y term premium (CA-US 10Y is also cheap at -111bp, 0.2nd percentile 1y, but the policy object is the front end). Marginal driver: post-hike SOFR/US 2Y versus a CORRA path that still leaves 2027 H1 CRA ~140bp below SR3.

historical_reference.distribution: CA-US 2Y -140bp: 3.77th percentile 1y, 4.31st percentile 5y, z_1y -1.84, z_5y -1.51 (as of 2026-09-17). Screen CA-US 2Y percentile 3.57, z -1.86. CA 2Y itself is 97.8th percentile 1y but only 58.5th percentile 5y; US 2Y is 99.8th percentile 1y and 88.0th percentile 5y. US 2s10s 25bp is 0.20th percentile 1y; CA 2s10s 56bp is 0.60th percentile 1y. AUDCAD 0.997577 is 99.8th/99.96th percentile 1y/5y and a 100th-percentile 1y screen, a commodity-peer FX flag of the same CAD cheapness, not the thesis.
analogs: Closest 2Y-spread LEVEL analog: 2025-01-30 CA-US 2Y at -145bp after a -17bp 1m move; forward +25bp over 3m (Canada cheapness compressed).
Same-move analog 2022-11-15 at -51bp: -4bp 1m / +6bp 3m (little convergence from a less extreme level).
US 2Y +57bp 1m analog 2022-09-16 at 3.85: +58bp 1m / +40bp 3m (US selloff continued), which is why the expression is RV rather than outright receive SOFR.
historical_reference.regime_differences: 2025-01 analog is the level match but predates this September Fed hike, BoC energy-pass-through minutes, and the 2026 energy-shock-absorber warning. 2022-11 was still in the post-COVID hiking cycle with a much narrower -51bp gap. Canada official zero curve is unavailable this packet, so sovereign 2Y is the historical yardstick and CORRA/SOFR futures are the live policy expression. NZ rates are unavailable, so NZ cannot be used as a second commodity-peer check.

independent_checks: Policy-path triangulation: 2027-03/06 strip averages are SOFR (4.58+4.72)/2=4.65 versus CORRA (3.13+3.365)/2=3.2475, a 140.25bp gap that matches CA-US 2Y -140bp rather than a bond-specific term-premium artifact.

Temperature gauges: Canada inflation 55 / labor 38 / activity 66 / consumer 45 versus US 72 / 75 / 69 / 74. Activity is close; the rate gap is much larger than the inflation-gauge gap. Labor is the genuine Canada-soft component and is treated as the main fundamental objection, not ignored.

FX/carry cross-check: USDCAD 1.401047 is 74th/87th percentile, not a 2Y-style extreme; AUDCAD is a 100th-percentile 1y screen with a 164.9bp 2Y differential, showing CAD cheapness versus another commodity peer, but 2Y carry of 140bp on USDCAD argues against using spot as the expression.

Positioning: CFTC TFF CAD leveraged-fund net -39022 contracts as of 2026-09-15, 99.0th percentile 1y, weekly change +16426 — funds are covering CAD shorts, so the cheap CA-US spread is not being created by an accelerating CAD liquidation.
context_build.flow_and_positioning_check: Verified: CAD futures OI 358186, 81.7th percentile 1y / 92.6th 3y, weekly +23325. Leveraged funds remain net short CAD but at the 99th percentile of their 1y net distribution and covering. AUD OI is 99th percentile 1y with leveraged funds net long, which can support rich AUDCAD but does not explain Canada rates remaining 140bp through US. CME positioning is unavailable (known gap). Inference: flow is not the primary driver of the CA-US rate gap; ownership is moving toward CAD even while the rate spread stays historically cheap. Unknown: dealer/official-curve plumbing in Canada because CA_official_curve is unavailable.

policy_path_check.rationale: This is a short-end US/Canada policy RV. Frozen CORRA (CRA) and SOFR (SR3) paths are available and are used as the tradable expression after inspecting policy_paths. A CA-US 2Y percentile is the historical anchor only; it is not a substitute for the STIR path.

trade.structure: Long locked linear combo: +1x SOFR futures_strip_average expiries 2027-03 and 2027-06 (SR3H7 4.58, SR3M7 4.72) versus -1x CORRA futures_strip_average expiries 2027-03 and 2027-06 (CRAH27 3.13, CRAM27 3.365), output_unit bps. Receive SOFR / pay CORRA. Curve family locked at open; do not migrate onto sovereign 2Y.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: CA-US 2Y is -140bp (4th percentile 1y and 5y); 2027 H1 SR3 minus CRA is about 140bp; overnight SOFR-CORRA is 156bp; Fed has hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00% with SOFR at 3.85; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through; Canada CPI 3%/core near 2%; US 2Y 4.76 is 99.8th percentile 1y while CA 2Y 3.27 is only 58th percentile 5y. Inference: that 140bp Canada discount is a peer-policy dislocation, not a fair labor-gap price, because activity gauges are close, energy pass-through is now in BoC deliberations, and the US front end has already done the post-hike rerating. Closest analog (2025-01-30 at -145bp) compressed 25bp over 3m. Unknown: whether Saudi Oman workaround fully caps the energy tail; CME positioning; Canada official curve. Trade is long SOFR-CORRA 2027 H1 to own compression of Canada cheapness.
trade.mispricing: Market prices a persistent ~140bp Canada discount through 2027 H1 (CRA 3.13/3.365 versus SR3 4.58/4.72) that matches a 4th-percentile CA-US 2Y. The fairer peer setting after a delivered Fed hike and BoC energy pass-through is a narrower 2027 H1 gap, with CORRA implied rates rising relative to SOFR.
why_now: Fed hike has printed and SOFR has jumped to 3.85; US 2Y is already 99.8th percentile 1y after +57bp in a month, so the US leg of the cheap Canada spread has run.
BoC minutes now flag energy pass-through while headline CPI is still 3%, a new transmission from a known inflation print into relative policy.
CA-US 2Y cheapened 15bp in five days (z -2.17) after a widely pre-priced FOMC, which is a new move that known Canada-soft labor does not by itself explain.
2027 H1 STIR still prints the same 140bp gap as the 2Y, so the historical dislocation is live in the tradable policy curve today, not only in a sovereign percentile.

Further Fed/global tightening confirmation (already-delivered hike, BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6-3 split) keeping US levels high while Canada catch-up remains incomplete.
